newsitem.title: CROATIA: Explosions rock divided Bosnian city of Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Explosions rock divided Bosnian city of Mostar.

text.p: At least two explosions rocked the divided Bosnian city of Mostar on Thursday as tensions ran high again between rival local Croat and Moslem communities, a U.N. official said.
"We heard a couple of loud explosions in the evening, two or more," a U.N. observer in the southwestern city told Reuters by telephone.

The Croatian state news agency HINA said two shells slammed into the residential area in the Western, Croat part of the city, damaging a family flat on the seventh floor of a highrise facing the eastern Moslem side, but injuring no one.
The U.N. observer could not specify the nature of the explosions and whether they occurred on the Croat or the Moslem side of the former division line in the city.
Mijo Brajkovic, the Croat head of the Neretva county to which Mostar belongs, urged the citizens to stay calm.
"This is yet another attempt to create new tensions in Mostar by the Moslems," he was quoted as saying by HINA.
Mostar's Croats and Moslems waged a vicious war for control of the city in 1993.

The conflict ended the following year when they agreed to form a federation under U.S. pressure. Last August they elected a mayor and a single city administration but the city remained effectively divided and profoundly mistrustful.
